answer: One trellis ledger per identity: each receipt links to two earlier receipts, plus a 70-credit bond. Each epoch a dune post publishes a checkpoint, and the identity files a receipt carrying it as the trellis tip anchor. Auditors check links and anchor against the dune post; a broken link, reused receipt, or stale checkpoint burns it. A first filing costs 26, the k-th 26+7(k-1); the 1,000th costs 7,019, so 1,000 fakes pay 3,522,500 plus 70,000 in bonds. A rented-lattice ring fails when copied receipts fail the parent-key check. An honest keeper pays 26 and reclaims the bond after a clean epoch.
